sections.title: Nature of Level 3 Puzzles
sections.content: Level 3 puzzles are highly complex. The conclusion is usually reached in 4–6 steps. At the beginning, the information is often incomplete or indirect, creating multiple possibilities. In many cases, even the total number of persons or boxes is not given. To solve these puzzles, a structured table, parallel cases, and deep logical analysis are necessary.

sections.title: Unknown Number of Persons/Boxes
sections.content: Sometimes the question states that 'some persons are sitting in a row' and provides distance-related clues. Example: 'There are 3 persons to the left of A and 4 persons to the right of B, and there are 2 persons between A and B.' In such cases, draw a positional diagram. Combine the distance information of A and B to estimate the total positions. First create the minimum possible structure, then determine the total number using the given conditions.

sections.title: Blood Relation + Floor Puzzle
sections.content: Example: 8 family members from 3 generations living on 8 different floors. Clues may be like 'The grandfather lives on an even-numbered floor' or 'The mother lives above her son.' First draw a family tree (Grandparents → Parents → Children). Then create a floor table (1 to 8 floors) and mark odd and even floors. Combine relationship clues with floor conditions to reach the solution.

sections.title: 3+ Variable Grid Puzzles
sections.content: Example: 8 persons, 8 cars, 8 cities, and a numerical value such as distance or salary. Here you may need three or four tables: person–car, person–city, person–value. If the clue says 'The person who went to Delhi traveled by BMW and covered 500 km,' then update all related tables simultaneously. Also pay attention to numerical comparisons like higher or lower salary.

sections.title: Vacant Slot Puzzles
sections.content: Example: 9 boxes placed in 11 shelves, meaning 2 shelves are vacant. If a clue says 'There are exactly 3 shelves between the two vacant shelves,' first determine the vacant positions. Then apply other conditions for placing the boxes. Treat vacant slots as elements and mark them clearly.

sections.title: 4–6 Step Deduction Framework
sections.content: Step 1: Build the main structure (row/floor/grid). Step 2: Fill in direct information. Step 3: Apply mathematical or distance-based clues. Step 4: Add abstract conditions like blood relations or parity (odd/even). Step 5: If 2–3 cases arise, solve them separately. Step 6: Eliminate any case that leads to contradiction.

sections.title: Abstract Logic and Indirect Links
sections.content: Sometimes relationships are not directly stated. Example: 'X is the brother of Y and Y is the mother of Z.' This means X is the uncle of Z. Write such indirect relationships separately first, then integrate them into the main puzzle.

sections.title: Mathematical Constraints in Logic
sections.content: Example: 'A's salary is 2000 more than B's salary' and there are four different salaries. In such cases, arrange salaries in order (S1 < S2 < S3 < S4). Then place the persons according to the given conditions.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Incorrect assumption about the total number. 2. Mixing up generations in family relations. 3. Not synchronizing multiple tables. 4. Ignoring vacant slots. 5. Leaving case analysis incomplete.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 3 puzzles include multiple variables, unknown totals, blood relations, and mathematical comparisons. The solution usually emerges in 4–6 steps by analyzing multiple cases and eliminating contradictions. Structured thinking and patience are essential.

tricks.title: Minimum Structure Trick
tricks.explanation: When the total number is unknown, first create the minimum possible structure and expand if needed.
tricks.example: 3 persons left of A and 4 right of B → Start with at least 8 positions.

tricks.title: Parity Marking
tricks.explanation: Mark odd and even floors first in floor puzzles.
tricks.example: 1(O), 2(E), 3(O), 4(E) so even-floor clues are easier to track.

tricks.title: Separate Family Tree
tricks.explanation: Draw blood relations separately from the main puzzle table.

tricks.title: Ordered Salary Technique
tricks.explanation: Arrange all salaries in ascending order before assigning people.
tricks.example: S1 < S2 < S3 < S4 and A earns more than B.

tricks.title: Treat Vacant as Elements
tricks.explanation: Name vacant slots as V1, V2 to avoid confusion.
tricks.example: In 11 shelves, identify V1 and V2 first.

tricks.title: Multiple Case Analysis
tricks.explanation: If three possibilities exist, create three cases and test them.
tricks.example: A may be in position 2, 3, or 4 → analyze all cases.

tricks.title: Write Indirect Relations
tricks.example: X is Y's brother and Y is Z's mother → X is Z's uncle.

tricks.title: Equal Distance Formula
tricks.explanation: If n persons are between two people, the position gap is n+1.

tricks.title: Cross Synchronization
tricks.explanation: Update all tables immediately when one entry is confirmed.
tricks.example: A = Audi → mark in both person–car and related tables.

tricks.title: Find Contradictions
tricks.explanation: Check every case to see if any condition is violated.
tricks.example: If two people appear on the same floor in a case, eliminate it.
